key_insight: Early Llama-3.1-8B layers best support word-level decoding from silent-reading EEG, while deeper layers increasingly capture passage-level context.
engineering_relevance: Target-layer selection offers a design dial for emphasizing word identity versus passage context in EEG language decoders.
method: Train a separate EEG-to-embedding decoder for each of 33 LLM layers.
Compare decoders with and without a causal transformer over EEG-window sequences.
Test context tracking using target-plus-noise and within-/across-session run-permutation controls.
evidence_signal: Using 19-channel silent-reading EEG, even a decoder processing one 0.5-second window at a time tracked passage context; controls indicated that most tracking followed the text rather than target geometry or session signatures.
watch_item: The abstract provides no sample size or numerical performance estimates, limiting assessment of robustness and practical decoding accuracy.
paper_title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
